ownership: benchmark fixture only; W1 owns world/faults and W2 owns VMM; no competing scheduler/device implementation

client_control.transport: stdin/stdoutUTF8 lines through reliable owned guest control device; independent of faultable Redis TCP
client_control.ready: oneJSON line phase=ready after warmup/dataset reconcile/replica WAIT; client then blocks readingSTART
client_control.start: START <guest monotonic epoch_ns> newline; epoch0 selects controlled current guest monotonic time
client_control.complete: oneJSON line phase=complete with canonical outcome+timing; failure phase=failed exit1
client_control.clock: guest System.nanoTime/Thread.sleep through pinned Linux/JVM clock profile; native clock permitted only in explicitly nondeciding native/local cases
client_control.W1_binding: coordinator maps reliable ingress/egress to ordered control messages; line framing is an application payload, not a replacement for W1 command framing

scenario.step: restore pinned whole-world post-warmup input; record restore cost
releaseSTART and collect epoch; ensure world mapping to epoch fixed by time policy
fault handle drops all primary<->replica frames; preserveTCP state; require drop counters/nonzero active partition traffic
release same fault handle; verify healed frame delivery and replica recovery
client issues BGREWRITEAOF as a separate admin command
client finishes fixed offered schedule, then WAIT/key verification/AOF completion
report actual drain; include it inend-to-end cost and fixed60s/host ratio; fail drain>5s

canonical_client_result: profile_id,seed,counts,replica-key checks,AOF completion and outcome_sha256; diagnostic host timing excluded from O1 witness
witness_normal: declared full future-relevant state at start/end and coarse checkpoints; coarse checkpoints are diagnostic coverage, not full boundary equality
witness_check: W3 boundary hash chain with declared CPU/KVM/RAM/world/device/control coverage; missing hidden state remains explicit
required_fault_evidence: replica catches up with all final model bytes
time_policy_inputs: native calibrated rational ns/conditional branch per workload profile
minimum 1ms link plus W1 safe horizon, zero-lookahead barriers and equal-time closure
scheduled device arrival, world-effect processing, legal IRQ acceptance and handler entry recorded separately

causal_progress.owner: W1 world scheduler; this benchmark does not implement an alternative scheduler
causal_progress.safe_horizon: minimum of known affecting deadlines and all producers' proven earliest unpublished effects plus guaranteed minimum path latency, with controller/shared-device zero-lookahead barriers and equal-time closure
causal_progress.frontiers: per-machine local frontiers and calibration remainders plus a world commit frontier; two machines reaching local 1ms advance the world to 1ms, not 2ms
causal_progress.known_deadlines: include pending frames, block completions, timers, faults, controller continuations and other effects that can affect the selected machine
causal_progress.producer_coverage: account for every active producer, including runnable guests, autonomous kernel/device work and controller actions, plus blocked-producer wake lower bounds, zero-latency paths and latency-reducing faults; an empty event queue alone is not a progress proof
causal_progress.slice_bound: end at or before the safe horizon and the declared 1ms maximum, possibly earlier; <=1ms alone does not prove exact causality
causal_progress.equal_time: process equal-time effects in W1's explicit stable order and close zero-lookahead effects/continuations before advancing beyond that time
causal_progress.arrival_vs_irq: scheduled device arrival and due world-effect processing remain exact. Linux IF/shadow restrictions may defer interrupt injection, acceptance or handler execution; that is guest semantics, not permission to defer due world work
causal_progress.error: advancing a guest past an unprocessed due world effect is a scheduling error, even if a later IRQ would be architecturally legal

device_timing_records.unobserved: null with explicit capture coverage; never infer guest IRQ acceptance or handler entry from the injection call alone
device_timing_records.interpretation: world processing past the due horizon is a scheduling error; IRQ acceptance/handler delay is reported separately with IF/shadow or other guest-semantic cause when observed

snapshot_pin: kernel/rootfs/JDK/jars/Redis/configs+whole-world state; shared env lock alone is not a runnable warmed snapshot
AMD_priority: no execution until coordinator hands benchmark breakdown the common hardware lock after W5a
